name: Raise 2048 solver avg score (expspawn retrain, no eval-seed overfit)

description: Baseline: shipped 128/32 net (base TD, 300k) on new held-out seed 9200, 20 games, 2-ply.

asi.note: seed 9200 is easier than 9000; use it for iteration only, confirm on 9300/9400

description: 1M-schedule base run: evaluated its ~210k checkpoint (lr still 0.0024), then annealed 70k more games at lr 0.0022. 2-ply stuck at ~76k with 0/20 8192 despite 1-ply recovering to 57.9k.

asi.cost: 1M run killed at ~210k after 52 min; anneal 70k = 926 s, 145.2M moves, 157k moves/s
asi.hypothesis: Stretching the built-in linear lr decay over 1M games would let more data pay off; a short late anneal from the mid-run checkpoint should recover the 300k-schedule quality.
asi.lesson: The 1M schedule keeps lr ~2x the 300k schedule at the same game count. A noisy V (high lr late) is usable for 1-ply greedy but poisons 2-ply max-over-second-moves: 1-ply 57.9k vs shipped 60.9k, but 2-ply 75.8k vs 134.9k. Annealing 70k from a noisy point does not fix the V ranking.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not stretch the decay; keep the shipped 300k schedule. Try train seed 2/3 at the same 300k recipe, and/or a faster-decay 400k run.
asi.result: 210k checkpoint at lr 0.0024 = 74.4k/10 games; +70k anneal to lr 2e-4 = 75.8k/20, 0/20 8192, 1-ply 57.9k. 2-ply did not recover.

description: Train seed 2 with the shipped 300k recipe (base, lr 0.003, par sqrt): diverged at 50,440/300,000 games

asi.cause: with train_games=300k the built-in decay gives lr 0.00255 at 50k, vs 0.00165 for the docs' 100k runs; seed 1 survives this, seed 2 does not
asi.failure: diverged at 50440/300000 games (non-finite or |w| > 1e6), not saving /tmp/base300k_s2c.bin; error: Diverged
asi.hypothesis: seed 2 at the shipped 300k schedule would give an independent sample of the same recipe
asi.lesson: the shipped 0.003 schedule sits at the stability edge; do not run seed 2 without a lower lr or a divergence guard
asi.next_action_hint: seed 3 only if a stable schedule is chosen; keep checkpoints

description: Train seed 1 300k at lr 0.002 (decay to 0.0002), evaluate the 250k checkpoint

asi.hypothesis: lr 0.002 for 300k would be more stable than 0.003 and give a better final V
asi.killed_at: 250000/300000 games by the 5400 s tool timeout
asi.lesson: lower lr undertrains at the same game budget; the shipped 0.003 schedule is better. This matches docs #135/#204 that game count and lr shape are already at the recipe's peak
asi.next_action_hint: do not lower the schedule lr to stabilize seeds; instead keep shipped lr and use checkpoints

description: SWA: average the last 4/8/16/32 checkpoints of a fresh 300k run and evaluate (best avg4 118,981.8)

asi.hypothesis: averaging nearby SGD checkpoints (SWA / Polyak averaging) smooths V and improves 2-ply ranking
asi.run: fresh 300k shipped-recipe run, killed at 285k; 57 unique checkpoints in /tmp/swa
asi.lesson: averaging raises 1-ply but destroys 2-ply, same signature as low-lr fine-tuning: the averaged V stops being the search-compatible value. SWA over 20k+ games is a dead end
asi.reproducibility: fresh 300k run does NOT reproduce shipped (116.9k at 285k vs 134.9k); nn.zig changed since the 2026-11-06 shipped net (#289/#321/#348), so each long run is a fresh sample with ~±6-8k variance; shipped may be a high draw
asi.caution: 4-point SWA sweep is a single run, not a controlled A/B
asi.next_action_hint: do not pursue checkpoint averaging; treat 134.9k as a high-variance target and require fresh-seed confirmation

description: phase_h6: full-width 3-ply only in the low-empty endgame (2-ply at >=4 empties). Seed 9200 +12.6k (147,442.8, 18/20 8192) looked strong, but seed 9300 paired diff was +10,801.8 +/- 10,050.1 and seed 9400 unpaired was +747.6 (134,452.8 vs 133,705.2, 8192 15/20 vs 16/20). No reliable score gain at 4.0-4.7x ms/move; 20-game seed noise is ~+/-10k.

asi.bugs_found: Phase.max_empty default must be 16 (empty 4x4 board); 15 caused an unreachable in phaseDepth for the .deep schedule. min_empty=3 alone also matches 4+ empties, so an 'exactly 3' row needs an upper bound.
asi.cost: 4.11 ms/move at 9200, 4.73 at 9400, 15.04 in the serial pairrow process; 3,852-3,935 leaves/move vs 980-986 for 2-ply
asi.dead_ends: 3-ply only at <=2 empties: 127,852.2 (-7k, 2.15x); sampled 2 spawns in the 3-ply tree: 60,533 (-74k, policy collapses); 3-ply only at exactly 3 empties: 4.29x cost, 119,384.8 on 5 games (the 3-empty root tree dominates cost).
asi.hypothesis: 3-ply expectimax restricted to <=3 empty cells buys the 8192 tail cheaply (between the shipped 2-ply and the 12.7x full 3-ply).
asi.next_action_hint: Stop tuning endgame depth; it is a cost curve, not a free win. If depth is revisited, add a min_max_tile condition so only 4096+ tail boards pay for 3-ply, and confirm with pairrow on 2 seeds.
asi.noise_floor: 20 games on one seed: ~+/-10k; identical recipe reruns at 300k differ by ~+/-8k (fresh 285k run = 116,965.8 vs shipped 134,867.2).
asi.why_rejected: The gain does not replicate on a third seed and is under 1.1 sigma on the paired seed; at 4x ms/move it fails the +20% latency budget and is not a real score improvement.

description: expspawn 40k with a 40k lr schedule, par + batch_scale 1.0: 37,552.4 avg2ply (13,447.6 1-ply, 0/20 8192), 1.30 ms/move. Far below the shipped 134,867.2 and below the documented serial 20k expspawn (61.6k); par+bs1 is 8x undertrained, so this does not refute expspawn, but it is unusable as run.

asi.hypothesis: expspawn (expected-spawn TD(0)) at 40k games with a 40k schedule reproduces the documented 20k win (61.6k vs base 30.7k) and scales toward the shipped net.
asi.measurement: 40,000 games, 21,457,408 moves in 1,033.7 s (20.8k moves/s) via par + batch_scale 1.0; final net 37,552.4 avg2ply, 13,447.6 avg1ply, 0/20 8192.
asi.why_it_failed: par + batch_scale 1.0 takes 8x fewer steps than serial (one merged step per 8 games with no scaling), so 40k games is only ~5k serial-equivalent games of training. The documented 20k expspawn run was serial (2,890 s, 5,977 moves/s), not par.
asi.prior_run: 300k expspawn at par bs1 ran 60k games in 22 min (~5 h total) and its 50k checkpoint (lr 0.00085) scored 44,141.8 / 1-ply 15,133.6; killed.
asi.next_action_hint: Only retry expspawn with the guard relaxed to allow par + batch_scale sqrt(8) (the base recipe's rule), so 40k games carry real update magnitude; compare against a base 40k run on the same eval. Without that, expspawn needs serial training, which is ~1.7 h per 40k games here.
asi.lesson: batch_scale is a step-size knob, not part of the target definition: the guard that rejects non-1 batch_scale forces either 8x undertraining (par bs1) or serial speed.
asi.noise_floor: 20 games on one seed ~+/-10k; 37.5k vs 61.6k is far outside that, so this is a real undertraining failure, not noise.

description: expspawn 40k, lr 0.001 with a 40k schedule, par + batch_scale sqrt(8) (guard relaxed to allow it): 46,458.8 avg2ply, 14,896.4 1-ply, 0.99 ms/move, +38% over base 40k (33,647.2). Still far below 134,867.2; establishes the budget slope for a 300k run.

asi.cost: 30,750,277 moves in 1,297.8 s (23.7k moves/s) via par + batch_scale sqrt(8)
asi.guard_change: expectedSpawnIsPlainTd1 now copies opts.batch_scale into the comparison, so par + sqrt(8) is accepted; everything else stays default.
asi.hypothesis: expspawn at 40k with par + batch_scale sqrt(8) (rather than 1.0) carries enough update magnitude to show the documented 2x edge over base.
asi.next_action_hint: Scale to 300k with par + sqrt(8) (about 1.8 h): 40k*2.83 = 106k serial-equivalent steps, still 2.83x under the shipped 300k, but expspawn's sample efficiency may close the gap. bs 8 (linear) is the exact match but risks the divergence seen at lr 0.003.
asi.result: +38% over base at the same budget (46,458.8 vs 33,647.2), but still 3x below the shipped 134,867.2 - consistent with the budget being far too small, not with a broken method.
asi.why_not_kept: Primary metric far below the shipped net; this run only establishes the training slope.

description: expspawn 300k at lr 0.001, par + batch_scale sqrt(8), killed at 190,000 games: 92,377.0 avg2ply, 43,855.8 1-ply, 5/20 8192, 1.92 ms/move. Trajectory 40k 46.5k -> 85k 75.3k -> 190k 92.4k; behind the current base recipe (~103k at 190k) and far below shipped 134,867.2, so not a candidate.

asi.hypothesis: expspawn scaled to 300k games with par + batch_scale sqrt(8) (106k serial-equivalent steps) closes the 40k-to-300k gap and beats the shipped 134,867.2.
asi.why_stopped: At 190k expspawn is already behind the current base recipe at the same budget (base 100k=82.6k, 300k=113.7k, so ~103k at 190k) and 42k short of the shipped net with only 110k games plus the final anneal left; the earlier +38% edge over base at 40k has inverted.
asi.cost: 190k games in ~3.2 h (~800 games/min, ~500 moves/game after 100k)
asi.next_action_hint: expspawn is closed for this machine: serial is 1.7 h per 40k games, par+bs1 is 8x undertrained, par+sqrt(8) scales worse than base after ~100k. Characterize the base recipe's seed-to-seed variance instead (seed 2 at lr 0.0028 to survive the 0.003 divergence; 300k base is only ~18 min).
asi.lesson: The Rao-Blackwellized target helps at small budgets (lower variance) but its bias/flatness hurts late: 1-ply 43.9k at 190k vs the base recipe's much sharper V, and 2-ply tracks the base at best.

description: Control: base 128/32, 300k games, lr 0.003, seed 1, par with the documented batch_scale sqrt(8)=2.8284271247461903: 108,899.0 avg2ply, 60,502.8 1-ply, 9/20 8192, 1.03 ms/move. Matches the shipped net's 1-ply but is 26k short at 2-ply; the shipped 134,867.2 is still not reproduced.

asi.control: Same recipe at batch_scale 1.0 (the `-` default) reached 116,965.8 at 285k on seed 9200 and 76.6k for seed 2 - so batch_scale 1.0 is not the sole explanation of the gap; the shipped net is ~20k above every rerun.
asi.hypothesis: The earlier reruns were 8x undertrained because `-` in the batch_scale slot means 1.0, not sqrt(8); rerunning the documented recipe with 2.8284271247461903 at 300k should reproduce the shipped net.
asi.next_action_hint: Rerun the recipe at the commit that last changed ai/solver/nn_weights.bin (#233, 2026-11-06) in a worktree; if that reproduces ~135k on seed 9200, the current training path regressed (or the old net is simply a high draw) and the old code is the base to improve from.
asi.result: 108,899.0 (1-ply 60,502.8 - now equal to the shipped 60,864.6 - and 9/20 8192 vs 15/20). The 1-ply parity with a 26k 2-ply deficit isolates the gap to the *deep* tail, not general V quality.
asi.runs: 300k total: 225k foreground (killed by the 2400 s tool timeout), then resume 75k at lr 0.001 decaying to 0.0001 (1,179 s).

description: Verification: retrained the shipped recipe from scratch (128/32, base, 300k games, lr 0.003, seed 1, par, batch_scale 2.8284271247461903) and got weights bit-identical to ai/solver/nn_weights.bin (sha256 match), hence the same 134,867.2. The training path is deterministic; earlier reproducibility/variance conclusions were caused by batch_scale 1.0 (`-`) runs being 8x undertrained.

asi.finding: The shipped 300k recipe is bit-for-bit deterministic on this machine: training seed 1 with base, lr 0.003, par, batch_scale sqrt(8) for 300k games reproduces ai/solver/nn_weights.bin exactly (sha256 c98ea27c...).
asi.invalidated: Earlier conclusions that the shipped net is an unreproducible high draw, and that 300k runs vary +/-8k, were artifacts of running `par - -` (batch_scale 1.0, 8x undertrained) or of resume/anneal splits. The 285k bs1 run (116.9k), the 40k base (33.6k), the seed-2 300k bs1 (76.6k) and the SWA experiment are all under-trained controls, not evidence about variance.
asi.lesson: `-` in the batch_scale slot means 1.0, not sqrt(batch): `parseBatchScale` returns 1.0 for `-`, and only args[12] can set 2.8284271247461903. Every par run must pass the value explicitly.
asi.next_action_hint: With a deterministic baseline, re-test the endgame 3-ply (h6) paired on seed 9000: re-add the phase_h6 mode (it was reverted in log #6), then pairrow A=row2 B=row28, 20 games. Only adopt if mean diff - 2*stderr > 0 and the 8192 count rises.
asi.verification: Eval on seed 9200 with the reproduced weights: 134,867.2, 1-ply 60,864.6, 15/20 8192, 5,716.2 moves, 0.98 ms/move - identical to the shipped-net baseline.

description: Endgame 3-ply (phase_h6) re-test with a paired run on the docs' seed 9000: A (2-ply) 141,548.0 vs B 144,256.0, mean diff +2,708.0 +/- 8,531.5 (10W/10L), 8192 18/20 vs 17/20, 3.9x leaves and 4x ms/move. Combined with 9200 +12.6k, 9300 +10.8k +/- 10.1k, 9400 +0.7k: no reliable gain, so the mode is reverted.

asi.conclusion: Endgame 3-ply is a wash: no seed shows a significant gain, and the cost is 4x ms/move. Search depth is closed unless the tree itself gets cheaper.
asi.cost: leaves/move 3,880.5 vs 952.3; 14.82 vs 3.67 ms/move in the serial pairrow process
asi.why_rejected: Only the 9200 unpaired run cleared the noise; two paired runs are within 0.3 sigma of zero and h6 even loses a 8192 game on 9000. At 4x latency it cannot be adopted.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not revisit phase depth without a cheaper tree (node TT associativity, a smaller leaf net) or a risk/tile condition that limits it to 4096+ boards. The V recipe is deterministic and already at its peak; the session has no measured lever above 134,867.2.

description: Enlarge the native node-TT from 4096 to 16384 entries in ai/solver/nn.zig: on the 3-ply row the score is bit-identical (146,470.7) while leaves drop 6.5% and ms/move 4.9%; the default 2-ply benchmark is unchanged at 134,867.2.

asi.hypothesis: A larger direct-mapped node cache raises the 3-ply hit rate and cuts leaf work at identical results.
asi.log_note: The cache is a deterministic memo; the score cannot change, only leaves/time.
asi.measured: Row 15 (3-ply with node TT default) 3 games seed 9200: score 146,470.7 both, leaves 10,251.5 -> 9,581.2 per move (-6.5%), ms/move 17.42 -> 16.57 (-4.9%), hit_rate 17.8%.
asi.next_action_hint: A 4-way associative 16k table (4k buckets x 4 ways) should raise the hit rate further; only pursue if the goal becomes shipping 3-ply.
asi.score_unchanged: Official benchmark after the change: avg2ply 134,867.2, 1-ply 60,864.6, 15/20 8192, 954.9 leaves/move, 1.00 ms/move - the 2-ply path never touches the node TT, so the primary metric is untouched.
asi.why_keep: No primary regression and a strict efficiency win on the opt-in 3-ply row; 768 KiB per thread native, wasm capacity unchanged at 1<<9.
